about: Review #471 A1 (lab PR 267): a root process staged in /tmp reads a GPG private key, connects out, then executes /usr/bin/dpkg in the same pid. In kernel order the read and the connect are judged before the dpkg exec; on the priority bus the exec (P1) is taken ahead of the queued read (P2) and connect (P3), and the package carve-out (`in_package_transaction`) read the later dpkg: CHAIN-002, CHAIN-007 and NET-008's kill went. The lineage is now read as of each event's time (`lineage::judged_at`): a package manager executed after the event covers nothing.

decision.name: /tmp exec then credential read then egress (3-step)
decision.reasoning: Process executed from a staging directory, then read a credential store, then opened an outbound flow — three-step dropper → credential-access → exfil chain (T1059 → T1555 → T1041); kill the process tree + posture → COMBAT [also matched: NN-L-CHAIN-001_CredReadThenEgress (KillProcessTree, Critical), NN-L-CHAIN-002_TmpExecThenEgress (KillProcessTree, Critical), NN-L-NET-008_OutboundFromTmpExec (KillProcess, High)] [judged at the connect, while the flow is open (lab PR 224)]
